Lul Tim on Rumored $1M Bounty on His Head for Killing King Von: Can You Collect It? (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, Lul Tim discussed the rumored $1 million bounty allegedly placed on his life following his involvement in the tragic death of rapper King Von. Tim took a defiant stance, questioning whether anyone who attempted to collect the bounty would make it back safely. He also revealed that his mother had to relocate due to threats, highlighting the severity of the situation and the precautions taken to protect his family.

Tim emphasized that his primary focus is self-defense, arguing that neither he nor Quando Rondo, who he said was facing a similar bounty, were the aggressors in the ongoing conflict. Despite continued criticism and speculation online, Tim maintained that he was focused on protecting himself and those close to him.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis Plans to Write the Judge on Lil Durk’s Behalf If He’s Found Guilty (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/EfhDHL5_UnU
--------
Judge Mathis sits down with DJ Vlad to discuss Lil Durk’s ongoing legal situation, emphasizing that he will respect the jury’s verdict while also acknowledging Durk’s community work in Chicago. Mathis explains why, if Durk is convicted, he intends to submit a letter to the court detailing their relationship, Durk’s efforts with his organization, record-clearing events for hundreds of felons, and his shift toward more positive music, including “All My Life.”

The conversation also covers King Von, Quando Rondo, Lul Tim, federal cases, and the broader impact of street conflicts on families and communities. Vlad and Mathis then examine high-profile pardons involving Bradford Cohen, Kodak Black, Lil Wayne, Emory Jones, Jay-Z, ROC Nation’s criminal justice work, Donald Trump, and the role fame and relationships can play in clemency.

recentItems.title: Norteño Shot Caller Mario Sanchez Predicts Lil Durk Gets Found Guilty, Too Many Snitches (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

--------
VladTV sits down with former Norteño figure Mario Sanchez, who weighs in on Lil Durk’s murder-for-hire trial as closing arguments unfold. Drawing from his own experience around prison politics, gang cases, and RICO prosecutions, Sanchez explains why he believes the presence of multiple informants and cooperating witnesses could make a guilty verdict likely. He also breaks down “guilty by association,” how juries may view testimony from admitted criminals, and why high-profile artists can face serious risk when street ties remain close.

The conversation also touches on Sanchez’s upcoming book, his San Francisco upbringing, prison years, success in mortgage banking, and rebuilding his life in Los Angeles. Vlad and Sanchez discuss loyalty, entourages, THF references, Lil Durk’s mainstream success with artists like Drake, Kanye West, and J. Cole, and the dangers of “bringing the block” into a new level of fame.

recentItems.title: Max B on How He Met Jim Jones (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/FoBBj-6j544
--------
In this VladTV interview, Max B breaks down the turbulent path that led him from New York arrests and parole violations to Harlem’s rap spotlight. He recalls early cases on 42nd Street, a robbery sentence, a $2 million bail, and the 2009 conviction that brought a 75-year sentence. While he was locked up, Harlem hip-hop exploded through Ma$e at Bad Boy, Cam’ron at Roc-A-Fella, Dipset, and the cultural impact of *Paid in Full* with Cam playing Alpo. Max explains how a chance encounter with Cam’ron, a missed studio link-up, and a 10-month return to prison sharpened his writing and helped create the “Max B” identity. After coming home, cousin Stan funded a new demo, which Bruno believed in and brought toward Jim Jones—setting the stage for Max’s entry into the rap business.

--------
Chingy sits down with VladTV to reflect on the business side of hip-hop, revealing that his first major deal at 22 with Ludacris’ Disturbing tha Peace (DTP) and Capitol Records came with only a $9,000 advance. The St. Louis rapper explains why he believes the contract was unfair, how publishing and mechanical royalties can impact young artists, and why knowing the business is essential.

The conversation also covers the Saint Lunatics’ reported reunion album with Metro Boomin, the ongoing tension involving Nelly, Ali, and Murphy Lee, and how money and ego have fractured major rap crews. Chingy compares those breakups to conflicts within G-Unit, Cash Money, No Limit, and other influential labels, while offering hard-earned advice to rising artists navigating managers, lawyers, touring, and contracts in today’s music industry.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis Wishes Lil Durk's People Didn't Want Revenge for King Von Getting Killed (Part 10)

Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------
Judge Mathis joins VladTV for a candid discussion about street culture, accountability, and the aftermath of King Von’s killing involving Quando Rondo’s circle. As Vlad raises questions about Lil Durk, alleged text messages, and whether any responsibility belongs to a culture of retaliation, Mathis says he wishes retribution wasn’t so deeply embedded in gang and street life. The conversation explores how emotion, adrenaline, and loyalty can override rational thinking, especially when violence is normalized.

They also examine why crimes are harder to escape in the modern era of cell phones, surveillance cameras, Ring cams, and digital evidence, while comparing today’s rap-related prosecutions to the 1980s. Mathis weighs in on claims of a “war on rap,” the use of lyrics in court, RICO cases targeting hip-hop, and high-profile legal battles involving Diddy and YNW Melly. Vlad also stresses the importance of strong legal representation in serious criminal cases.

recentItems.title: Lawyer Bradford Cohen on How He Got Lil Wayne a Pardon from Trump (Part 3)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 2: https://youtu.be/2rKwQ07Tr-A
Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------
Attorney Bradford Cohen sits down with Vlad to discuss his close relationships with high-profile clients, from Kodak Black to Lil Wayne. Cohen reflects on Kodak’s loyalty, his generosity in donating 170 air conditioners to Golden Acres during a heat wave, and the bond that inspired Kodak’s lyric, “I told my lawyer, boy, I love you like my daddy.” The conversation then turns to Lil Wayne’s federal gun case and the presidential pardon granted by Donald Trump. Cohen explains that he was not Wayne’s original attorney on the case, crediting Miami lawyer Howard Srebnick, but later handled pardon paperwork after Wayne had met with Trump about the Platinum Plan for urban communities, a policy also discussed publicly with Ice Cube. Cohen shares why Trump’s awareness of social media, press coverage, and public support may have played a role in cases involving major cultural figures.

--------
Charleston White sits down with Vlad to react to the federal case against Daejon Love, the alleged NFL impostor accused of posing as a San Francisco 49ers player and scamming 26 women out of $1.3 million. Vlad breaks down claims that Love used fake football imagery, a supposed contract signing, and FaceTime investment pitches with an alleged financial advisor to convince women to take out loans and send money.

White responds with his trademark provocative humor, comparing online deception to everyday dating misrepresentations, including fake hair, fake credentials, and exaggerated lifestyles. The conversation also touches on wire fraud, conspiracy charges, restitution, social media fakery, relationship dynamics, and the blurred line between “game” and criminal fraud.

The interview closes with jokes about Love needing a book or a “How to Be a Player” remake, referencing Bill Bellamy’s classic comedy. Watch the full VladTV exchange for the complete discussion.

recentItems.title: Moe Gangat on Dolph Family Rejecting Hernandez Govan’s Plea Deal Before Not Guilty Verdict (Part 8)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 7: https://youtu.be/hl6zPLY-_GI
Part 1: https://youtu.be/fjE20W3ouPQ
--------
Moe Gangat joins VladTV to break down a surprising turn in the Young Dolph murder case involving Hernandez Govan, who says he signed a 10-year plea deal before prosecutors brought it to Dolph’s family and the offer was rejected. Vlad revisits his interview with Govan and defense attorney Manny Arora, explaining how the case went to trial after the deal fell apart — and ended with a not guilty verdict. Gangat analyzes the unusual influence a victim’s family can have in plea negotiations, the role of the Memphis DA, and why Arora’s courtroom win could raise his profile in criminal defense circles. The conversation also touches on Govan’s connection to the Memphis music scene, the emotional impact on Young Dolph’s family, and the broader questions around justice, prosecution strategy, and hip-hop-related criminal cases.
